decisive_items: Several round atrophic lesions on his face, symmetric and bilateral
The skin lesions were not indurated and displayed no epidermal changes
Orcein stain demonstrated reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis beneath the epidermal dell
response.rationale: Round atrophic facial lesions without induration or epidermal changes, with dermal fibrosis, superficial lymphocytic infiltrate, and reduced elastic fibers on orcein staining are characteristic of atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini. Other candidates imply inflammation, epidermal alteration, granulomatous, or vasculitic histology.

rejected.why: Follicular atrophoderma would require follicular involvement or epidermal changes; the lesions are non-follicular round atrophic plaques with no epidermal changes described.
Sarcoidosis requires granulomas and typically indurated lesions; histology here shows lymphocytic infiltrate, fibrosis, and elastic-fiber loss, not granulomas.
Discoid lupus erythematosus typically has epidermal changes such as scaling and follicular plugging, and prior inflammation; both are denied.
Erythema elevatum diutinum is a vasculitic nodular/plaque disease, not non-inflammatory atrophic lesions.
Lupus erythematosus broadly requires interface/epidermal changes and inflammation, which are absent.
Dermatomyositis presents with proximal muscle weakness and characteristic rashes, not isolated atrophic facial lesions.
Lichen sclerosus shows epidermal atrophy and sclerosis, usually anogenital, contradicting no epidermal changes and non-indurated lesions.
Follicular mucinosis shows follicular mucinous degeneration and alopecia, not elastic-fiber loss with dermal fibrosis.
